title: AI Brain — A Personal Intelligence and Memory System
description: Build a secure personal AI Brain that connects multiple data sources, maintains long-term memory, understands user context and relationships, and proactively suggests useful actions. The system should retrieve relevant information from connected sources, provide context-aware responses, and execute tasks only after user approval.

title: EvoArena — Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Gaming Environment
description: Build an interactive reinforcement learning gaming environment where autonomous AI agents learn, compete, cooperate, and evolve strategies through self-play and environmental interaction. The platform should support procedurally generated maps, dynamic challenges, adaptive opponents, and multi-agent coordination. It should demonstrate measurable learning improvements and the ability to generalize strategies to previously unseen environments through an interactive training and performance dashboard.

title: "Acoustic-Alchemist": Non-Verbal Audio & Environmental Trigger System
description: A real-time audio classification and DSP pipeline that reacts to non-speech acoustic events—like beatboxing, whistling pitch, finger snaps, or table drumming—to control creative software or games.
prerequisites: Deep Learning for audio (1D/2D CNNs or RNNs in PyTorch/TensorFlow)
rough_roadmap: Set up a low-latency sliding-window microphone stream and implement background noise profiling/subtraction.
Record and augment a custom dataset of non-verbal acoustic triggers (snaps, claps, beatbox kicks/hi-hats, whistles) alongside ambient room noise.
Extract real-time Mel-spectrograms/MFCCs and train a lightweight CNN classifier + pitch/onset detector for continuous inference.
Build a state-machine router that maps acoustic triggers and pitch variations to application controls (e.g., a rhythm-strategy game, live loop station, or hands-free coding macros).
Optimize inference latency, add a live spectrogram HUD, and test robustness in noisy environments.
learning_outcomes: Real-time acoustic stream processing, spectral feature extraction, and noise suppression
Training custom audio classification models on spectrogram representations without relying on speech-to-text APIs
Designing low-latency audio buffer pipelines for interactive human-computer control
A fully voice/sound-driven game or creative software tool operable via non-verbal acoustics

title: Foley-Craft: Vision-to-Audio Procedural Soundscape Engine
description: A multimodal system that watches silent video clips, live webcam feeds, or gameplay screens and dynamically generates or mixes a synchronized, multi-layered soundtrack and sound-effects landscape in real time.
prerequisites: Computer Vision fundamentals (OpenCV, Optical Flow, Object Detection)
Digital Signal Processing (DSP) basics and audio manipulation libraries (Librosa, PyAudio, Pydub, or Pygame.mixer)
Familiarity with pre-trained scene/emotion classification models
rough_roadmap: Build the video ingestion pipeline to extract frame-by-frame visual metrics (dense/sparse optical flow for motion speed, color histograms, and object bounding boxes).
Design the state-mapping logic that translates visual telemetry (e.g., sudden motion spikes or bounding-box overlaps) into musical parameters (tempo, intensity, volume envelopes, SFX triggers).
Construct the real-time audio mixing and synthesis engine capable of crossfading stems, modulating BPM, and triggering low-latency impact sound effects.
Build an interactive visualizer UI to display live visual telemetry alongside audio waveforms and genre/mood controls.
Test across diverse silent video inputs (e.g., corridor sprints, gameplay footage) and package the final demo.
learning_outcomes: Cross-modal translation between computer vision telemetry and procedural audio synthesis
Real-time optical flow calculation, collision heuristics, and visual scene analysis
Programmatic audio mixing, DSP manipulation, and low-latency audio buffer management
A working procedural soundscape engine with an interactive control dashboard

title: Zero-Text Multimodal Desktop Search
description: A local, visual-first "Second Brain" search engine for messy image folders, lecture screenshots, and meme dumps that lets users search by vibe, rough sketch, color palette, or visual similarity.
rough_roadmap: Build the local directory indexer that scans image folders, extracts OCR text, computes dominant color palettes, and generates CLIP/SigLIP vision embeddings.
Set up a local vector index (FAISS) for sub-millisecond cross-modal retrieval (text-to-image, image-to-image, and sketch-to-image).
Implement dimensionality reduction (UMAP/t-SNE) and clustering to project the entire image library into 2D/3D coordinates grouped by visual theme/vibe.
Build an interactive frontend featuring a 2D/3D embedding galaxy explorer, a live sketch-pad query tool, and semantic search filters.
Optimize batch indexing speed (ONNX/FP16 quantization), add duplicate detection, and record a demo on a chaotic multi-thousand-image dataset.
learning_outcomes: Working with contrastive multimodal embeddings (CLIP/SigLIP) and cross-modal retrieval pipelines
Vector database indexing (FAISS) and high-dimensional data visualization using UMAP/t-SNE
Combining OCR, color-space heuristics, and semantic vectors into a unified hybrid search engine
A fast, local multimodal desktop search application with an interactive 3D embedding explorer

title: ProofGraph — Autonomous AI Evidence Intelligence Engine
description: Build an autonomous AI investigation platform where specialized agents independently research information, verify factual claims, challenge unreliable findings, detect contradictions, and validate evidence against original sources. The platform should construct an interactive knowledge graph connecting claims, sources, supporting evidence, and conflicting findings to generate transparent research reports with traceable citations and uncertainty assessments.

title: Shadow-Boxer: Full-Body Kinetic Controller
description: A real-time, zero-controller human-computer interface that uses webcam pose estimation, hand landmarks, or facial mesh tracking to control interactive games, simulations, or desktop workspaces.
prerequisites: Familiarity with pre-trained pose/landmark models (MediaPipe, YOLO-Pose)
Basic understanding of time-series smoothing or simple neural networks (MLP/LSTM)
rough_roadmap: Set up the webcam capture pipeline and integrate MediaPipe/YOLO-Pose for real-time skeletal and facial landmark extraction.
Implement temporal smoothing filters (e.g., One-Euro or Kalman filter) to eliminate landmark jitter and stabilize coordinates.
Build the gesture recognition engine—starting with geometric heuristics and upgrading to a custom temporal sequence classifier over frame buffers.
Map recognized states to low-latency OS input events (<100ms) and connect the pipeline to a target game or interactive application.
Polish the visual overlay HUD, fine-tune responsiveness, and record a live gameplay demo.
learning_outcomes: Real-time spatial computing and human-centric computer vision pipeline engineering
Low-latency asynchronous frame processing and temporal signal smoothing
Training custom sequence classifiers on spatial keypoint buffers
End-to-end functional kinetic controller with a playable live demonstration

title: Scalpel: Weight-Space Programming, Editing a Neural Network's Weights with an LLM
description: Build an LLM agent that changes another network's behaviour by directly editing its weights from a natural-language goal, with no gradient descent. Inspired by MIT CSAIL's "Sparks of Weight-Space Programming" (2026)
prerequisites: Transformer architecture and mechanistic interpretability basics
LLM APIs and agent tool use
rough_roadmap: Pre-register hypothesis, build model zoo and gradient-free edit sandbox
Toy MLP and small-policy edits, with and without tools
Small-LM edits plus baselines (LoRA, steering, ROME, random)
Side-effect and mechanism analysis, verdict and paper
learning_outcomes: A NeurIPS-style paper on a brand-new research direction

title: Pocket: Distilling a Large Agent into a Small Model That Runs on a Laptop
description: Distill a strong teacher model's multi-step agent trajectories into a ≤2B student model, then quantize it so it runs locally. Measure how much of the teacher's success survives, and at what cost and speed.
rough_roadmap: Improvement beyond plain imitation (DAgger / recovery / DPO)
bit quantization, local deployment, error analysis and demo
learning_outcomes: Knowledge distillation and imitation learning for agents
A laptop-runnable agent with a benchmark report

title: Doodle-2-Dungeon: Sketch-to-Interactive World Pipeline
description: A physical-to-digital pipeline that takes a hand-drawn 2D paper sketch of a level layout, circuit, or wireframe and compiles it into a playable game level, physics sandbox, or working web app.
prerequisites: Python and JavaScript/Game Engine basics (Pygame, Godot, Three.js, or HTML5 Canvas)
Classical Computer Vision (OpenCV thresholding, morphological operations, Canny edges, contour hierarchies)
Convolutional Neural Networks (PyTorch/TensorFlow) for custom symbol classification
Data augmentation techniques for small image datasets
rough_roadmap: Build the OpenCV preprocessing pipeline (grayscale conversion, adaptive thresholding, perspective/homography warping, and contour extraction to isolate individual drawn components).
Curate and augment a dataset of hand-drawn symbols representing level elements (walls, hazards, spawn points, coins) and train a lightweight CNN/ViT classifier.
Convert spatial bounding boxes, contour geometry, and classified labels into a structured intermediate JSON level schema.
Build the game/sandbox parser that reads the JSON schema and instantiates playable physics objects, collision meshes, and custom segmented sprites.
Add live camera/upload UI, refine classification accuracy under varied lighting, and record end-to-end paper-to-playable demos.
learning_outcomes: Hybrid pipelines combining classical OpenCV morphological processing with deep learning classifiers
Dataset curation, synthetic augmentation, and training custom CNNs from scratch
Homography estimation and spatial coordinate mapping from 2D images to interactive engines
An end-to-end compiler that turns physical paper drawings into playable digital environments

title: SwarmFlow — Multi-Agent Task Coordination Engine
description: Build an intelligent multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized AI agents collaborate to complete complex tasks. The system should automatically divide tasks, assign responsibilities, share progress, resolve conflicting decisions, and recover from failures through a centralized supervisor agent. It should produce one verified and consolidated final deliverable.
